info.desc: Rumours is the eleventh studio album by British-American rock band Fleetwood Mac. Largely recorded in California during 1976, it was produced by the band with Ken Caillat and Richard Dashut and was released on 4 February 1977 by Warner Bros. Records. The record peaked at the top of both the main United States Billboard chart and the United Kingdom Albums Chart. "Go Your Own Way", "Don't Stop", "Dreams", and "You Make Loving Fun" were released as singles. A Grammy Award winner, Rumours is Fleetwood Mac's most successful release with sales of over 40 million copies worldwide, and diamond certifications in .

podcast.body: In a 2007 retrospective, Patrick McKay described *Rumours* as a "safe middle ground" for pop music bands, positioned between punk rock (like Richard Hell) and conventional music. Critic Robert Christgau praised it, noting its role in reminding listeners that "rock and roll is supposed to be about pleasure as well as all the heavy stuff" during the "year of the punk." Conversely, critic Robert Hilburn found its weakest moments to be "a nutritionist nightmare 16 zillion calories and no substance," criticizing its sweet but "unfulfilling" vocals and "muted" guitar work compared to their live performances. Despite some initial critical reservations, it has become one of the best-selling albums of all time, cherished for its "near musical flawlessness" and lyrics that deeply resonated with listeners, particularly "boomers" navigating divorce in the late 1970s. podcast.body: Released in 1977, this album is described as being "packed with beef" and more accurately a "collection of diss tracks aimed at each other," rather than just a soap opera about romantic entanglements. It documents the bandmates' romantic breakups and interpersonal grievances, with several key songs directly targeting other members. "Rumors is commonly called a soap opera. A drama fueled by the bandmates' romantic breakups and entanglements. Actually, it's more aptly called a collection of diss tracks aimed at each other."

podcast.body: The recording of the Rumours album was famously fraught with internal romantic entanglements and widespread infidelity among band members, which has been extensively documented. Despite the complex personal relationships, the band managed to remain together for several years afterward, a period that must have been considerably awkward, potentially aided by substance use. "The canoeedling that went on in Fleetwood Mac during the recording of the rumors album has been documented many times. Legendary, everybody seemed to be fooling around with everybody else."

podcast.body: This album began taking shape even before the promotional cycle for its 1975 predecessor concluded. Recording was notoriously difficult due to romantic breakups among all five band members, including divorces and relationship splinters. Despite the dramatic backstory not being widely known initially, the LP shot to number one in just six weeks by early April 1977. It spent a staggering 31 weeks at number one, making it the third longest run on top in chart history, behind "West Side Story" soundtrack and Michael Jackson's "Thriller." It is certified for 20 million copies in the US alone and roughly double that worldwide. "When rumors arrived in February 1977, the dramatic backstory of the album wasn't widely disseminated in the press yet, but the LP shot to number one in just six weeks, quite fast in the days before computerized charts."

podcast.body: This album is described as a blockbuster, with its success fueled by the band's infamous internal drama, including fractious breakups, betrayals, recriminations, addictions, and soap opera-quality plot twists. The album's songs conveyed the highly charged perspectives of its three independent-minded singer-songwriters: Stevie Nicks, Lindsey Buckingham, and Christine McVie. "The Fractious Breakups, Betrayals, Recriminations, Addictions, and Soap Opera quality plot twists that helped make 1977's Rumors album A Blockbuster."

This classic LP from 1977 made history as the first act to pull four top ten hits from a single album. These hits included "Go Your Own Way" (#10), "Dreams" (#1), "Don't Stop" (#3), and "You Make Loving Fun" (#9). "In 1977, their classic rumors LP generated the number ten hit go your own way, the number one dreams, the number three don't stop, and the number nine you make loving fun."
